etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English scateren, skateren, (also schateren, see shatter), from Old English *sceaterian, probably from a dialect of Old Norse. Possibly related to Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to cut, split, shatter”). Compare Middle Dutch scheteren (“to scatter”), Low German schateren, Dutch schateren (“to burst out laughing”); and is apparently remotely akin to Ancient Greek σκεδάννυμι (skedánnumi, “scatter, disperse”). and Tocharian B kät- (“to scatter, sow seeds”). Doublet of shatter.

definitions.definition: (ergative) To (cause to) separate and go in different directions; to disperse.

quote.citation: c. 1588–1593 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Lamentable Tragedy of Titus Andronicus”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene ii]:
quote.text: Scatter and disperse the giddy Goths.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To distribute loosely as by sprinkling.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “The Third Book of the Georgics”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Why should my muse enlarge on Libyan swains, / Their scattered cottages, and ample plains?

quote.citation: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Chasca planetary description:
quote.text: Chasca's ring is unique. It appears to be, for lack of a better term, a massive piece of alien "installation art." The rings are made of small pieces of synthetic material, and are almost invisible from space. From the ground, they catch and scatter the light of Matano in picturesque ways. It is not known who created the ring or when.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To occur or fall at widely spaced intervals.

quote.citation: 2016, J. D. Vance, Hillbilly Elegy, page 21:
quote.text: […]  its beauty is obscured by the environmental waste and loose trash that scatter the countryside.

definitions.definition: (transitive, baseball) Of a pitcher: to keep down the number of hits or walks.
The act of scattering or dispersing.
